chunks: "Whoever casts the pebbles at the Jamarat, with each pebble a major destructive sin is removed from him. And when the believer casts it, the angel catches it; and when the disbeliever casts it, Satan says, 'With your buttocks, you did not throw.'"

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan, mentioned here in a mocking response
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the Jamarat, the ritual stone-pillars pelted during hajj
key_terms.الْكَافِرُ: the disbeliever whose act lacks acceptance
key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: the angel who catches the pebble
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer whose act is spiritually received
key_terms.حَصَاةٍ: a pebble used in the rite of stoning

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of casting the pebbles at the Jamarat in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the spiritual merit of casting the pebbles at the Jamarat during hajj. It teaches that this ritual act brings the removal of grave sins for the believer and highlights the difference between sincere faith and disbelief in the acceptance of worship.
